subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun's Big Mela Shop Adventure
hook: Arjun counts toys at the village fair and discovers how big numbers help us read price tags.

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: curious student who loves solving number puzzles

characters.name: Priya
characters.role: Arjun's clever friend who notices patterns in numbers

slides.title: The Big Toy Shop
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Priya visit a mela (fair) with a toy shop. The shopkeeper says there are 3,247 toys in the store!

points.label: Setting
points.text: A busy village fair in Delhi with colourful toy stalls

slides.inSimpleWords: Arjun sees a HUGE number at the toy shop.

image.alt: The Big Toy Shop — Numbers up to 10000

slides.title: Place Value: Thousands
slides.storyContext: The shopkeeper explains: 3,247 means 3 thousands, 2 hundreds, 4 tens, and 7 ones. Priya draws it out.

points.label: 3 thousands
points.text: 3,000 — three full bags of 1,000 toys each

points.label: 2 hundreds
points.text: 200 — two boxes of 100 toys

points.label: 4 tens
points.text: 40 — four bundles of 10

points.label: 7 ones
points.text: 7 — single toys

slides.inSimpleWords: Each digit holds a different place value.

image.alt: Place Value: Thousands — Numbers up to 10000

slides.title: Breaking Down a Price
slides.storyContext: A remote-control car costs ₹5,432. Arjun wants to write it in words and in parts.

example.problem: Write 5,432 in expanded form and in words.
example.solution: 5,432 = 5,000 + 400 + 30 + 2 = Five thousand, four hundred thirty-two

slides.inSimpleWords: Split the number by its place values.

image.alt: Breaking Down a Price — Numbers up to 10000

slides.title: Comparing Numbers
slides.storyContext: Priya notices the doll collection has 2,890 dolls and the action figure stall has 3,150. Which is bigger?

points.label: Compare thousands first
points.text: 2 thousands vs 3 thousands → 3 is bigger

points.label: So 3,150 > 2,890
points.text: The action figure stall has more

slides.inSimpleWords: Compare the leftmost (biggest place) first.

image.alt: Comparing Numbers — Numbers up to 10000

slides.title: Ordering Numbers
slides.storyContext: Arjun lists four game prices: ₹1,200, ₹1,500, ₹900, ₹2,000. He arranges them from smallest to largest.

example.solution: 900 < 1,200 < 1,500 < 2,000 (smallest to largest)

slides.inSimpleWords: Line up numbers from tiny to huge.

image.alt: Ordering Numbers — Numbers up to 10000

slides.title: Rounding to the Nearest 10, 100, 1000
slides.storyContext: The shopkeeper says the toy count is 'about 3,250' but Priya knows it's actually 3,247. She rounds for quicker counting.

points.label: Nearest 10
points.text: 3,247 → 3,250 (7 is closer to 10 than 0)

points.label: Nearest 100
points.text: 3,247 → 3,200 (47 is closer to 0 than 100)

points.label: Nearest 1000
points.text: 3,247 → 3,000 (247 is closer to 0 than 1000)

slides.inSimpleWords: Round by looking at the next digit.

image.alt: Rounding to the Nearest 10, 100, 1000 — Numbers up to 10000

slides.title: The Missing Price Tag
slides.storyContext: A new toy arrives with a price of _,456 rupees. The first digit fell off! Priya knows it must be between 2,000 and 3,000.

points.label: Problem
points.text: If the price is between ₹2,000 and ₹3,000, what can the first digit be?

example.problem: Find the missing digit: _,456 is between 2,000 and 3,000
example.solution: The digit must be 2. So the price is ₹2,456.

slides.inSimpleWords: Use limits to find a hidden digit.

image.alt: The Missing Price Tag — Numbers up to 10000

slides.title: The Mela Champion Shopkeeper
slides.storyContext: By sunset, Arjun and Priya can read any price tag in the entire mela. They help the shopkeeper count all the money: ₹7,890 in notes and ₹1,256 in coins.

points.label: Celebration
points.text: They understand numbers up to 10,000 and can solve real-world problems!

slides.inSimpleWords: Numbers help us count and shop wisely.

image.alt: The Mela Champion Shopkeeper — Numbers up to 10000

slides.title: What We Learned
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Priya remember their mela lessons about place value, comparison, rounding, and real-world maths.

points.label: Place value
points.text: Thousands, hundreds, tens, ones

points.label: Compare
points.text: Always look at the biggest place first

points.label: Round
points.text: Use the next digit to decide up or down

points.label: Apply
points.text: Use these skills to read prices and count money

slides.inSimpleWords: Big numbers are just small numbers grouped smartly.

image.alt: What We Learned — Numbers up to 10000

subject: Mathematics
title: Priya Discovers the Ancient Library
hook: Priya reads book numbers written as I, V, X and learns a 2,000-year-old number system.

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: helps Priya decode the mystery of old number marks

characters.name: Priya
characters.role: discovers Roman numerals on ancient library shelves

slides.title: The Old Library Mystery
slides.storyContext: Priya visits her grandmother's library and finds books marked VI, XII, VIII. She wonders why they don't use normal numbers.

points.label: Setting
points.text: An old Delhi library with ancient books and dusty shelves

slides.inSimpleWords: Priya finds mysterious symbols on book spines.

image.alt: The Old Library Mystery — Roman Numerals

slides.title: The Basic Roman Symbols
slides.storyContext: Grandmother explains the five main symbols used for 2,000 years by Romans and still used today.

points.label: I
points.text: means 1 — like one finger

points.label: V
points.text: means 5 — like an open hand

points.label: X
points.text: means 10 — like two hands crossed

points.label: L
points.text: means 50 — an ancient Roman shape

points.label: C
points.text: means 100 — from the word 'Centum' (hundred)

slides.inSimpleWords: Five symbols build all Roman numbers.

image.alt: The Basic Roman Symbols — Roman Numerals

slides.title: Reading Simple Numbers
slides.storyContext: Arjun points to a book marked IVIII (4) and another marked VII (7). Priya counts the sticks.

example.problem: Read these Roman numbers: III, VI, VIII

slides.inSimpleWords: Add symbols from left to right.

image.alt: Reading Simple Numbers — Roman Numerals

slides.title: The Subtraction Rule
slides.storyContext: Grandmother shows a special trick: IV (4) doesn't mean 6; it means 5 minus 1 because I comes before V!

points.label: IV = 4
points.text: I (1) before V (5) means subtract: 5−1=4

points.label: IX = 9
points.text: I (1) before X (10) means subtract: 10−1=9

points.label: XL = 40
points.text: X (10) before L (50) means subtract: 50−10=40

points.label: XC = 90
points.text: X (10) before C (100) means subtract: 100−10=90

slides.inSimpleWords: A smaller symbol before a bigger one means subtract.

image.alt: The Subtraction Rule — Roman Numerals

slides.title: Subtraction in Action
slides.storyContext: Priya reads Volume IV (4) and Volume IX (9) from a series. She writes out both using subtraction.

example.problem: Decode: IV, IX, XL

slides.inSimpleWords: Smaller left of bigger means minus.

image.alt: Subtraction in Action — Roman Numerals

slides.title: Writing Numbers Up to 100
slides.storyContext: Arjun learns that XII is 10+1+1=12, and XIX is 10+(10−1)=19. Priya writes her age, 14, as XIV.
slides.inSimpleWords: Combine addition and subtraction rules.

image.alt: Writing Numbers Up to 100 — Roman Numerals

slides.title: Mystery Book Dates
slides.storyContext: The library books have publication years written in Roman numerals. One book is MDCCCXVII. Priya breaks it down.

points.label: Problem
points.text: M=1000, D=500, C=100. What year is MDCCCXVII?

example.problem: Decode MDCCCXVII

slides.inSimpleWords: Learn M (1000) and D (500) for bigger years.

image.alt: Mystery Book Dates — Roman Numerals

slides.title: The Roman Numerals Are Everywhere!
slides.storyContext: Walking home, Arjun spots Roman numerals on a clock, on monument stones, and even on school buildings. Priya realizes they're timeless.

points.label: Real-world use
points.text: Clock faces, movie titles, building plaques, book volumes

slides.inSimpleWords: Roman numerals live in our modern world.

image.alt: The Roman Numerals Are Everywhere! — Roman Numerals

slides.title: Roman Numeral Recap
slides.storyContext: Priya and Arjun summarize their adventure through centuries of numbers.

points.label: Addition
points.text: Add symbols left to right

points.label: Subtraction
points.text: Smaller left of bigger = subtract

points.label: Real use
points.text: Clocks, books, dates, monuments

slides.inSimpleWords: Ancient Romans gave us a clever number code.

image.alt: Roman Numeral Recap — Roman Numerals

subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun's Cricket Ball Factory
hook: Arjun groups cricket balls to prepare for a tournament and learns multiplication and division shortcuts.

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: runs a cricket ball factory and learns fast counting

characters.name: Priya
characters.role: organizes teams and shares balls fairly

slides.title: The School Tournament
slides.storyContext: The school cricket tournament is starting! Arjun's job is to prepare 6 boxes, each with 8 cricket balls. Priya helps organize.

points.label: Challenge
points.text: How many balls total? Counting one by one takes too long!

slides.inSimpleWords: Arjun needs a faster way to count groups.

image.alt: The School Tournament — Multiplication and Division

slides.title: Multiplication as Repeated Addition
slides.storyContext: Instead of adding 8+8+8+8+8+8, Priya shows Arjun a shortcut: 6 times 8 = 6 × 8.

points.label: Shortcut
points.text: 6 × 8 = 48 (multiply instead of add)

points.label: Fast!
points.text: One multiplication beats six additions

slides.inSimpleWords: Multiply to count equal groups quickly.

image.alt: Multiplication as Repeated Addition — Multiplication and Division

slides.title: Multiplying by Groups
slides.storyContext: Arjun sees his factory has 4 warehouses with 7 boxes each. How many boxes total?

example.problem: 4 warehouses × 7 boxes each = ? boxes

slides.inSimpleWords: Groups × items per group = total items.

image.alt: Multiplying by Groups — Multiplication and Division

slides.title: Division as Sharing Equally
slides.storyContext: Now 48 balls must be shared equally among 6 cricket teams. Priya divides: 48 ÷ 6 = how many per team?

points.label: Total
points.text: 48 balls

points.label: Teams
points.text: 6 teams

points.label: Each team gets
points.text: 48 ÷ 6 = 8 balls

points.label: Check
points.text: 6 × 8 = 48 ✓ (multiplication and division are opposites)

slides.inSimpleWords: Division splits a big group into equal parts.

image.alt: Division as Sharing Equally — Multiplication and Division

slides.title: Division in Action
slides.storyContext: A factory machine makes 36 cricket bats. Arjun packs them into 9 sets (one per team). How many bats per set?

example.problem: 36 bats ÷ 9 sets = ? bats per set
example.solution: 36 ÷ 9 = 4 bats per set. Check: 9 × 4 = 36 ✓

slides.inSimpleWords: Share the total fairly into groups.

image.alt: Division in Action — Multiplication and Division

slides.title: Multiplication Tables (Up to 10 × 10)
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches Arjun the 3, 4, 5, 6 times tables so he can multiply without counting fingers.

points.label: Know them by heart
points.text: Speeds up all maths and problem-solving

slides.inSimpleWords: Memorize key multiplication facts.

image.alt: Multiplication Tables (Up to 10 × 10) — Multiplication and Division

slides.title: The Mixed-Up Order
slides.storyContext: A delivery truck brings 120 new cricket balls. Arjun must pack them into bags of 8 or 10. How many full bags each way? Are there leftovers?

points.label: Problem
points.text: 120 ÷ 8 = ? and 120 ÷ 10 = ? Which leaves no remainder?

example.problem: Divide 120 balls: into bags of 8 OR bags of 10?
example.solution: 120 ÷ 8 = 15 bags (no remainder). 120 ÷ 10 = 12 bags (no remainder). Both work!

slides.inSimpleWords: Check if numbers divide evenly.

image.alt: The Mixed-Up Order — Multiplication and Division

slides.title: Tournament Day Success
slides.storyContext: The tournament begins. All 6 teams have exactly 8 cricket balls each. Arjun's factory is a success, and he never counted one by one!

points.label: Victory
points.text: Multiplication and division saved time and solved the problem perfectly

slides.inSimpleWords: Smart maths solved the real-world challenge.

image.alt: Tournament Day Success — Multiplication and Division

slides.title: Multiplication & Division Mastered
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Priya celebrate their mastery of these powerful shortcuts.

points.label: Multiply
points.text: Count equal groups fast

points.label: Divide
points.text: Share fairly into groups

points.label: Opposites
points.text: Multiply and divide undo each other

points.label: Tables
points.text: Know times facts to solve instantly

slides.inSimpleWords: Multiplication and division are speedy math superpowers.

image.alt: Multiplication & Division Mastered — Multiplication and Division

subject: Mathematics
title: Priya's Chocolate Cake Party
hook: Priya bakes a cake, cuts it into pieces, and learns fractions and decimals by sharing with friends.

characters.name: Priya
characters.role: bakes cakes and discovers fractions through sharing

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: helps measure recipe ingredients and split portions

slides.title: The Birthday Cake Bake
slides.storyContext: Priya bakes a big chocolate cake for her birthday. She cuts it into 8 equal slices. Arjun eats 2 slices. What fraction did he eat?

points.label: Setup
points.text: One whole cake, 8 equal pieces, Arjun takes 2 pieces

slides.inSimpleWords: Fractions show parts of something whole.

image.alt: The Birthday Cake Bake — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: Understanding Fractions
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: the bottom number (8) tells you how many equal parts. The top number (2) tells you how many parts Arjun got.

points.label: Numerator (top)
points.text: 2 — the pieces Arjun got

points.label: Denominator (bottom)
points.text: 8 — total equal slices

points.label: Fraction
points.text: 2/8 (two-eighths) of the cake

slides.inSimpleWords: Top = parts taken, bottom = total parts.

image.alt: Understanding Fractions — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: Fractions in Real Cakes
slides.storyContext: Priya cuts another cake into halves (2 parts). Arjun eats 1 half. She cuts a third cake into quarters (4 parts) and Arjun gets 1 quarter.

example.problem: Name the fractions: 1 half, 1 quarter, 2 halves
example.solution: 1/2 (one-half), 1/4 (one-quarter), 2/2 = 1 whole (two halves)

slides.inSimpleWords: Halves, thirds, quarters are common fractions.

image.alt: Fractions in Real Cakes — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: Comparing Fractions
slides.storyContext: Priya has 1/4 cake left. Arjun has 1/2 cake left. Who has more?

points.label: Same numerators
points.text: 1/4 vs 1/2 — smaller denominator = bigger piece
Half is bigger than a quarter

points.label: Tip
points.text: Smaller bottom number = bigger actual piece

slides.inSimpleWords: Smaller bottom means a bigger slice.

image.alt: Comparing Fractions — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: Intro to Decimals
slides.storyContext: Arjun measures milk for the frosting: 0.5 litres (half a litre) and 0.25 litres (a quarter). Decimals use points, not fractions!

points.label: Decimal point
points.text: The dot (.) separates whole from parts
Same as 1/2 (five-tenths)
Same as 1/4 (twenty-five hundredths)
One-tenth of a whole
One-hundredth of a whole

slides.inSimpleWords: Decimals show parts using a point.

image.alt: Intro to Decimals — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: Fractions and Decimals Together
slides.storyContext: Priya reads a recipe: 3/4 cup sugar (same as 0.75 cup). She uses 1/2 cup flour (same as 0.5 cup). Arjun writes both ways.

example.problem: Write as both fraction and decimal: 3/4, 1/2, 1/10

slides.inSimpleWords: Fractions and decimals are two ways to say the same part.

image.alt: Fractions and Decimals Together — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: The Cake Sharing Problem
slides.storyContext: Priya bakes 3 cakes. Each has 8 slices. She gives 2/8 to Arjun, 3/8 to a friend, and keeps 1/8. How many slices are left unsold?

points.label: Problem
points.text: Total 24 slices. 2/8 + 3/8 + 1/8 = 6/8. How many remain?

example.problem: 24 slices − (2/8 + 3/8 + 1/8) = ? slices left

slides.inSimpleWords: Add fractions and subtract from the total.

image.alt: The Cake Sharing Problem — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: The Party Success
slides.storyContext: Priya's birthday party is perfect. Everyone gets a fair share: Arjun gets 1/4, friend gets 1/3, family gets the rest. Fractions made sharing fair and fun!

points.label: Lesson
points.text: Fractions and decimals help us divide, measure, and share wisely in everyday life

slides.inSimpleWords: Fair sharing needs fractions and decimals.

image.alt: The Party Success — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: Fractions & Decimals Recap
slides.storyContext: Priya and Arjun recap their delicious discovery.

points.label: Fractions
points.text: Top = parts taken, bottom = total parts (e.g., 2/8)

points.label: Common fractions
points.text: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 3/4 appear everywhere

points.label: Decimals
points.text: Use a point: 0.5, 0.25, 0.75 = same as fractions

points.label: Use it
points.text: Cooking, measuring, sharing, money

slides.inSimpleWords: Fractions and decimals split whole things fairly.

image.alt: Fractions & Decimals Recap — Fractions and Decimals

subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun's Garden Design
hook: Arjun designs a school garden using rectangles, circles, and triangles, then builds 3D structures.

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: plans the garden layout using shapes and angles

characters.name: Priya
characters.role: calculates area and perimeter for planting

slides.title: The Garden Plan
slides.storyContext: The school wants a beautiful garden. Arjun is in charge of design. He uses a big rectangle for the main plot, circles for flower beds, and triangles for shade structures.

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Draw and measure shapes to use space wisely

slides.inSimpleWords: Shapes help plan and build gardens.

image.alt: The Garden Plan — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: 2D Shapes: Sides and Angles
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches Arjun about flat (2D) shapes: a rectangle has 4 sides and 4 right angles (90°). A triangle has 3 sides and 3 angles.

points.label: Rectangle
points.text: 4 sides, 4 right angles (90°), opposite sides equal

points.label: Triangle
points.text: 3 sides, 3 angles, many types (right, equilateral, isosceles)

points.label: Circle
points.text: No sides, no angles, all points same distance from centre

points.label: Square
points.text: Special rectangle: 4 equal sides, 4 right angles

slides.inSimpleWords: Shapes have sides and angles.

image.alt: 2D Shapes: Sides and Angles — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: Calculating Perimeter
slides.storyContext: Arjun's main garden plot is a rectangle: 8 metres long, 5 metres wide. He needs to fence it. How much fencing does he need?

example.problem: Rectangle 8m × 5m. What's the perimeter (distance around)?
example.solution: Perimeter = 2(length + width) = 2(8+5) = 2(13) = 26 metres of fencing needed

slides.inSimpleWords: Perimeter = add all the sides.

image.alt: Calculating Perimeter — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: Calculating Area
slides.storyContext: Priya asks: how much soil do we need for the garden? We measure the AREA (space inside), not just around it.

points.label: Area of rectangle
points.text: length × width = 8 × 5 = 40 square metres

points.label: Area of square
points.text: side × side; for 5m side: 5 × 5 = 25 square metres

points.label: Area of triangle
points.text: 1/2 × base × height

points.label: Square metres
points.text: Unit for measuring area (m²)

slides.inSimpleWords: Area = space inside a shape.

image.alt: Calculating Area — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: Designing Flower Beds
slides.storyContext: Arjun designs three flower bed shapes: a square (4m × 4m), a triangle (base 6m, height 4m), and a circle (radius 3m).

example.problem: Find the areas: Square 4×4, Triangle base 6 height 4, Circle radius 3
example.solution: Square: 4×4=16 m²; Triangle: 1/2×6×4=12 m²; Circle: 3.14×3²≈28 m²

slides.inSimpleWords: Different shapes need different area formulas.

image.alt: Designing Flower Beds — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: 3D Shapes (Objects with Volume)
slides.storyContext: For shade, Arjun plans a small hut. That's a 3D shape! A cube (box), a cone, and a cylinder are common 3D shapes.

points.label: Cube
points.text: 6 square faces, 8 corners, all sides equal (dice shape)

points.label: Cuboid (box)
points.text: 6 rectangular faces, length, width, height differ

points.label: Sphere
points.text: Ball-shaped, no flat faces, no corners

points.label: Cylinder
points.text: Two circular faces, curved surface (tin can shape)

points.label: Cone
points.text: One circular base, one point at top (ice cream cone)

slides.inSimpleWords: 3D shapes have volume (thickness).

image.alt: 3D Shapes (Objects with Volume) — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: The Garden Structure
slides.storyContext: Arjun's shade hut is a cube with 2m sides. He needs to know the volume (how much air inside). What's the volume?

points.label: Problem
points.text: A cube hut: 2m × 2m × 2m. What's the volume?

example.problem: Volume of a cube with 2m sides = ?
example.solution: Volume = side × side × side = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 cubic metres (m³)

slides.inSimpleWords: Volume = space inside 3D shapes.

image.alt: The Garden Structure — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: The Garden Grand Opening
slides.storyContext: The garden is built! A rectangle of soil (40 m²), circle flower beds (28 m²), triangle shade areas, and a cube hut (8 m³). Arjun's geometry design is perfect!

points.label: Success
points.text: Geometry made the garden beautiful, organized, and functional

slides.inSimpleWords: Shapes turn plans into real gardens.

image.alt: The Garden Grand Opening — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: Geometry Mastered
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Priya celebrate their shape skills.

points.label: 2D shapes
points.text: Rectangles, triangles, circles (flat, no thickness)

points.label: Perimeter
points.text: Distance around a shape

points.label: Area
points.text: Space inside a shape (square metres)

points.label: 3D shapes
points.text: Cubes, spheres, cylinders (have volume)

points.label: Use it
points.text: Building, designing, planning, architecture

slides.inSimpleWords: Geometry helps us design and measure our world.

image.alt: Geometry Mastered — Geometry Shapes

subject: Science
title: Arjun's Space Adventure
hook: Arjun and Priya zoom through the solar system and visit each planet to learn about our cosmic neighbourhood.

characters.name: Priya
characters.role: navigator with a star map and endless questions

slides.title: Blast Off to Space!
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Priya hop into a rocket at Earth's south pole. They're heading to explore the eight planets orbiting our Sun.

points.label: Setting
points.text: A spacecraft in orbit, with Earth and the Sun visible below

slides.inSimpleWords: The solar system is our home in space.

image.alt: Blast Off to Space! — The Solar System

slides.title: The Sun: Heart of Our System
slides.storyContext: The Sun is enormous, burning hot, and everything orbits it! Arjun feels the warmth even from this distance.

points.label: The Sun
points.text: A giant ball of burning gas (star), gives light and heat

points.label: Size
points.text: 109 times wider than Earth; we could fit 1.3 million Earths inside!

points.label: Energy
points.text: All life on Earth depends on the Sun's energy

points.label: Age
points.text: About 4.6 billion years old (middle-aged for a star)

slides.inSimpleWords: The Sun is a giant fire ball that rules our system.

image.alt: The Sun: Heart of Our System — The Solar System

slides.title: The Eight Planets
slides.storyContext: Priya points to her star map. There are 8 planets, ordered by distance from the Sun. Mercury is closest and hottest; Neptune is farthest and coldest.

points.label: Close planets
points.text: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars (small, rocky, inner)

points.label: Far planets
points.text: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune (huge, icy or gassy, outer)

points.label: Earth
points.text: Our home! Just right for life (water, air, perfect temperature)

points.label: No Pluto
points.text: Pluto was demoted to a 'dwarf planet' in 2006

slides.inSimpleWords: Eight planets orbit the Sun in order.

image.alt: The Eight Planets — The Solar System

slides.title: Mercury to Mars: The Inner Planets
slides.storyContext: Arjun's ship zooms past the inner rocky planets. Mercury is tiny and scorching (450°C!). Venus is thick with clouds. Earth is perfect. Mars is red and cold.

example.problem: Why is Earth special but Mercury and Venus are not?
example.solution: Earth has liquid water, breathable air, and moderate temperature. Mercury is too hot, Venus's atmosphere crushes everything.

slides.inSimpleWords: Rocky planets near the Sun are too harsh for Earth life.

image.alt: Mercury to Mars: The Inner Planets — The Solar System

slides.title: The Gas Giants: Jupiter and Saturn
slides.storyContext: Priya sees Jupiter, the HUGE gas giant with red storms. Then Saturn, with its beautiful rings made of ice and rock.

example.problem: Jupiter is 11 times wider than Earth. How many Earths fit inside Jupiter?
example.solution: About 1,300 Earths fit inside Jupiter! (volume is 11³ times bigger)

slides.inSimpleWords: Gas giants are enormous, not solid, with many moons.

image.alt: The Gas Giants: Jupiter and Saturn — The Solar System

slides.title: The Moon: Earth's Faithful Friend
slides.storyContext: As they return, Arjun and Priya orbit Earth and marvel at the Moon. It orbits Earth, causes tides, and lights our night sky.

points.label: The Moon
points.text: Earth's natural satellite, orbits us every 27 days

points.label: Tides
points.text: Moon's gravity pulls Earth's oceans, creating high and low tides

points.label: Phases
points.text: New moon, crescent, half moon, full moon (Earth sees different lit parts)

points.label: Distance
points.text: About 384,000 km away (still our nearest neighbour)

slides.inSimpleWords: The Moon dances around Earth every month.

image.alt: The Moon: Earth's Faithful Friend — The Solar System

slides.title: Asteroid Belt Mystery
slides.storyContext: Between Mars and Jupiter, millions of rocks float in an asteroid belt. Priya asks: how did this belt form?

points.label: Challenge
points.text: The asteroid belt might be pieces of a planet that never formed. Why?

example.problem: What might have prevented a planet from forming in the asteroid belt?
example.solution: Jupiter's strong gravity scattered and prevented rocks from clumping together to form a planet.

slides.inSimpleWords: The asteroid belt is cosmic rubble.

image.alt: Asteroid Belt Mystery — The Solar System

slides.title: Home Sweet Earth
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Priya land back on Earth. Looking up at the night sky, they see the Moon and planets they visited. Earth suddenly feels precious and unique.

points.label: Realization
points.text: Our planet is a rare jewel in a vast solar system

slides.inSimpleWords: Earth is special, and we must care for it.

image.alt: Home Sweet Earth — The Solar System

slides.title: The Solar System Recap
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Priya chart their adventure and what they learned.

points.label: The Sun
points.text: Giant star at the centre, gives light and heat

points.label: 8 Planets
points.text: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars (inner rocky); Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune (outer giant)

points.label: The Moon
points.text: Earth's satellite, causes tides, lights the night

points.label: Why Earth?
points.text: Water, air, right temperature = perfect for life

points.label: Explore
points.text: There is so much more to discover in space!

slides.inSimpleWords: The solar system is our cosmic home to explore.

image.alt: The Solar System Recap — The Solar System

subject: Science
title: Priya's Playground Physics Lesson
hook: Priya discovers forces and motion by playing on swings, slides, and in races with Arjun.

characters.name: Priya
characters.role: curious student experimenting with forces on the playground

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: helps measure speeds and predict motion

slides.title: The Playground Mystery
slides.storyContext: Priya is playing on the school playground. She pushes a swing. Why does it move? Why does it eventually stop? Arjun joins and they investigate.

points.label: Questions
points.text: What makes things move? What stops them? Why does a ball roll differently on grass vs concrete?

slides.inSimpleWords: Forces control motion all around us.

image.alt: The Playground Mystery — Force and Motion

slides.title: What Is a Force?
slides.storyContext: A force is a push or pull. Priya pushes the swing. Gravity pulls objects down. Friction slows them. These are all forces!

points.label: Push
points.text: You shove a ball across the floor

points.label: Pull
points.text: You tug a rope toward you

points.label: Gravity
points.text: Pulls everything downward to Earth

points.label: Friction
points.text: The rubbing force that slows sliding things

slides.inSimpleWords: Forces are pushes or pulls that change motion.

image.alt: What Is a Force? — Force and Motion

slides.title: Forces on the Slide
slides.storyContext: Priya climbs the slide and sits at the top. Gravity pulls her down (a force). As she slides, friction from the plastic creates heat and slows her a bit.

example.problem: Name the forces acting on Priya sliding down: gravity and friction. Which wins?
example.solution: Gravity pulls down harder than friction resists, so Priya accelerates. If the slide were water-slick, less friction → faster slide.

slides.inSimpleWords: Gravity pulls down; friction slows the slide.

image.alt: Forces on the Slide — Force and Motion

slides.title: Motion and Speed
slides.storyContext: Arjun races Priya 100 metres across the playground. Arjun runs 100 m in 10 seconds. Priya takes 12 seconds. Who is faster?

points.label: Speed
points.text: How fast something moves (distance per time)

points.label: Winner
points.text: Arjun is faster (higher speed)

slides.inSimpleWords: Speed = distance ÷ time.

image.alt: Motion and Speed — Force and Motion

slides.title: Calculating Speed
slides.storyContext: A ball rolls down the playground slope. It travels 5 metres in 2 seconds. What's its speed?

example.problem: Ball rolls 5 m in 2 seconds. Speed = ?
example.solution: Speed = distance ÷ time = 5 m ÷ 2 s = 2.5 m/s

slides.inSimpleWords: Divide distance by time to find speed.

image.alt: Calculating Speed — Force and Motion

slides.title: Newton's First Law: Things Keep Doing What They Do
slides.storyContext: Priya rolls a ball. Once moving, it keeps rolling (slowly) until friction stops it. Once still, it stays still unless pushed.

points.label: Objects at rest
points.text: Stay at rest (stopped ball stays stopped)

points.label: Objects in motion
points.text: Stay in motion unless a force stops them (rolling ball keeps rolling)

points.label: Friction
points.text: The invisible force that eventually stops all motion

points.label: Inertia
points.text: Things resist change in motion

slides.inSimpleWords: Things resist changing their motion.

image.alt: Newton's First Law: Things Keep Doing What They Do — Force and Motion

slides.title: The Skateboard Skid
slides.storyContext: A skateboard rolls at 4 m/s on smooth concrete. Then it enters sand. Friction increases, and it stops in 5 seconds. How far did it slide?

points.label: Problem
points.text: Initial speed 4 m/s, friction slows it. Average speed? Distance?

example.problem: Skateboard at 4 m/s enters sand and stops in 5 s. Distance = ?
example.solution: Average speed = (4 + 0) ÷ 2 = 2 m/s. Distance = average speed × time = 2 × 5 = 10 m

slides.inSimpleWords: Friction slows motion by removing energy.

image.alt: The Skateboard Skid — Force and Motion

slides.title: Playground Physics Master
slides.storyContext: Priya and Arjun now see forces and motion everywhere: in kicks, throws, swings, slides, and races. They are playground physicists!

points.label: Insight
points.text: Physics is not just textbooks—it's happening every moment we play

slides.inSimpleWords: Science explains how our world moves.

image.alt: Playground Physics Master — Force and Motion

slides.title: Force and Motion Recap
slides.storyContext: Priya and Arjun review their playground discoveries.

points.label: Force
points.text: A push or pull that changes motion

points.label: Common forces
points.text: Gravity (pulls down), friction (resists motion), pushes, pulls

points.label: Speed
points.text: Distance ÷ time

points.label: Motion law
points.text: Things keep moving or staying still unless a force changes them

points.label: Real world
points.text: Sports, driving, flying—all controlled by forces

slides.inSimpleWords: Forces make things move or stop.

image.alt: Force and Motion Recap — Force and Motion

subject: Science
title: Arjun Traces Water's Journey
hook: Arjun follows a water droplet from the ocean through clouds and rain, learning the water cycle.

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: follows water droplets through their epic journey

characters.name: Priya
characters.role: explains each stage of the water cycle with diagrams

slides.title: A Droplet's Adventure Begins
slides.storyContext: Arjun imagines he's a tiny water droplet in the Arabian Sea. The hot sun beats down. He's about to go on the wildest journey ever!

points.label: Setting
points.text: Ocean near the coast of India, in early summer heat

slides.inSimpleWords: Water journeys across land, sky, and sea forever.

image.alt: A Droplet's Adventure Begins — The Water Cycle

slides.title: Evaporation: Becoming Water Vapor
slides.storyContext: The Sun's heat warms the ocean, and Arjun-the-droplet rises into the air as invisible water vapor. This is EVAPORATION.

points.label: Evaporation
points.text: Liquid water turns into invisible water vapor gas

points.label: Heat source
points.text: The Sun provides energy to lift water into the air

points.label: From water surfaces
points.text: Oceans, lakes, rivers, soil, plants all evaporate

points.label: Invisible
points.text: You can't see water vapor, but it's everywhere in air

slides.inSimpleWords: Heat turns water into invisible vapor.

image.alt: Evaporation: Becoming Water Vapor — The Water Cycle

slides.title: Evaporation Happens Everywhere
slides.storyContext: Priya does an experiment: she places wet clothes on a line in the sun. By evening, they're dry! Where did the water go?

example.problem: Why do wet clothes dry in the sun?
example.solution: The Sun's heat evaporates the water in the fabric into invisible vapor in the air.

slides.inSimpleWords: Sun heats water and turns it to vapor.

image.alt: Evaporation Happens Everywhere — The Water Cycle

slides.title: Condensation: Vapor Becomes Clouds
slides.storyContext: High in the sky, the air is cold. Arjun-the-vapor cools down and condenses into tiny water droplets, joining billions of others to form a cloud.

points.label: Condensation
points.text: Invisible water vapor cools and turns into liquid water droplets

points.label: Temperature drop
points.text: High in atmosphere, air is cold, so vapor condenses

points.label: Droplet formation
points.text: Tiny dust particles in air help water vapor condense

points.label: Clouds
points.text: Billions of water droplets clustered together

slides.inSimpleWords: Cold air turns vapor into water droplets (clouds).

image.alt: Condensation: Vapor Becomes Clouds — The Water Cycle

slides.title: See Condensation Now
slides.storyContext: Arjun breathes on a cold mirror. It fogs up! That fog is condensation—his warm breath vapor hitting the cool glass and turning to liquid.

example.problem: Why does a mirror fog when you breathe on it?
example.solution: Your breath contains warm water vapor. The cool mirror surface causes it to condense into tiny liquid droplets, creating the fog.

slides.inSimpleWords: Vapor cools and becomes visible water droplets.

image.alt: See Condensation Now — The Water Cycle

slides.title: Precipitation: Rain and Snow
slides.storyContext: In the cloud, Arjun's droplet collides with others. They stick together and get heavy. So heavy they can't float! They fall as rain.

points.label: Precipitation
points.text: Water falls from clouds as rain, snow, sleet, or hail

points.label: Rain
points.text: Droplets fuse and become too heavy; they fall (most common)

points.label: Snow
points.text: High altitude: vapor condenses into ice crystals instead of droplets

points.label: Monsoon
points.text: India's summer rains (July–September) bring tons of precipitation

slides.inSimpleWords: Heavy water droplets fall as rain or snow.

image.alt: Precipitation: Rain and Snow — The Water Cycle

slides.title: The Complete Water Cycle
slides.storyContext: Arjun falls as rain on the Himalayas, flows into rivers, and eventually reaches the ocean again. He traces the FULL cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection.

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Draw or describe all four stages of the water cycle in order.

example.problem: A raindrop falls on a mountain, flows to a river, ends in the ocean. Name the water cycle stages.
example.solution: 1. Precipitation (rain falls). 2. Collection (flows into ocean). 3. Evaporation (Sun heats ocean). 4. Condensation (vapor cools, forms cloud). Repeat!

slides.inSimpleWords: Water cycles forever: ocean → sky → rain → ocean.

image.alt: The Complete Water Cycle — The Water Cycle

slides.title: Arjun Completes the Cycle
slides.storyContext: As rain, Arjun nourishes crops, fills wells, powers rivers. He realizes water is incredibly precious and shared globally—every drop counts!

points.label: Insight
points.text: The same water has been cycling for 4.5 billion years; we are drinking water ancient dinosaurs drank

slides.inSimpleWords: Water is ancient, precious, and endlessly recycled.

image.alt: Arjun Completes the Cycle — The Water Cycle

slides.title: The Water Cycle Recap
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Priya review the eternal journey of water.

points.label: Evaporation
points.text: Sun heats water → invisible water vapor rises

points.label: Condensation
points.text: Cool air turns vapor → liquid droplets in clouds

points.label: Precipitation
points.text: Droplets fuse and fall as rain, snow, sleet

points.label: Collection
points.text: Water pools in oceans, lakes, rivers, soil

points.label: Repeat
points.text: The cycle never ends; same water, forever renewed

slides.inSimpleWords: Water journeys endlessly: heat, rise, cool, fall, collect.

image.alt: The Water Cycle Recap — The Water Cycle

subject: Science
title: Priya's Journey Through the Digestive System
hook: Priya imagines she's a piece of food and travels through the body, learning how we digest and get energy.

characters.name: Priya
characters.role: explores the digestive system from mouth to intestines

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: explains organs and enzymes that break down food

slides.title: A Rice Grain's Adventure
slides.storyContext: Priya pretends to be a grain of rice at the breakfast table. She's about to take an incredible journey through a human body!

points.label: Setting
points.text: A typical Indian breakfast table with rice, dal, and vegetables

slides.inSimpleWords: Food travels through your body in a wild journey.

image.alt: A Rice Grain's Adventure — Human Body and Digestion

slides.title: The Mouth: First Stop
slides.storyContext: Priya enters Arjun's mouth. Teeth chew her into tiny bits. Saliva (spit) mixes in and starts breaking her down chemically.

points.label: Teeth
points.text: Chop and crush food into small pieces (mechanical digestion)

points.label: Saliva
points.text: Enzyme in saliva begins to break down starch (chemical digestion)

points.label: Tongue
points.text: Pushes chewed food around and helps swallowing

points.label: Time in mouth
points.text: 15–30 seconds of chewing begins the digestive work

slides.inSimpleWords: Chewing and spit start breaking down food.

image.alt: The Mouth: First Stop — Human Body and Digestion

slides.title: Chewing Matters
slides.storyContext: Arjun chews 32 times for each bite. Priya realizes: the more he chews, the easier her journey will be!

example.problem: Why does chewing slowly help digestion?
example.solution: Smaller pieces mean more surface area for enzymes to work on. Saliva breaks down carbs before the food leaves the mouth.

slides.inSimpleWords: Chew thoroughly to help your digestion.

image.alt: Chewing Matters — Human Body and Digestion

slides.title: The Esophagus and Stomach
slides.storyContext: A muscular tube (esophagus) pushes Priya down into the stomach, a muscular bag where her journey truly intensifies.

points.label: Esophagus
points.text: Muscular tube pushes food down (15–20 seconds)

points.label: Stomach
points.text: Churns food + releases stomach acid + proteases (proteins break down)

points.label: Stomach acid
points.text: Strong chemical that kills germs and breaks down proteins

points.label: Time in stomach
points.text: 2–4 hours of churning and chemical breakdown

slides.inSimpleWords: Stomach acid churns food into paste.

image.alt: The Esophagus and Stomach — Human Body and Digestion

slides.title: Why Stomach Acid Doesn't Dissolve Us
slides.storyContext: Priya wonders: if stomach acid is so strong, why doesn't it digest the stomach itself? Arjun explains the protective lining.

example.problem: Stomach acid is powerful. Why doesn't it eat through the stomach wall?
example.solution: The stomach wall has a thick mucus lining that protects it from acid. This special layer shields the stomach tissue.

slides.inSimpleWords: A slime lining protects your stomach from its own acid.

image.alt: Why Stomach Acid Doesn't Dissolve Us — Human Body and Digestion

slides.title: The Small Intestine: Absorption Powerhouse
slides.storyContext: Now a paste, Priya enters the small intestine, a long coiled tube where the REAL magic happens—nutrients are absorbed into the bloodstream!

points.label: Length
points.text: About 6–7 metres long, but coiled tightly in the belly

points.label: Bile from liver
points.text: Breaks down fats

points.label: Pancreatic juice
points.text: Enzymes break down carbs and proteins

points.label: Villi
points.text: Tiny finger-like structures in the intestine that absorb nutrients

points.label: Nutrients absorbed
points.text: Glucose, amino acids, fats, vitamins enter the blood

slides.inSimpleWords: Small intestine absorbs nutrients into the blood.

image.alt: The Small Intestine: Absorption Powerhouse — Human Body and Digestion

slides.title: Tracking Nutrients
slides.storyContext: Priya (the rice grain) has been converted to glucose. She enters a villus and crosses into the bloodstream. Arjun asks: where does she go next?

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Blood carries glucose to cells for energy. Which body parts need the most glucose?

example.problem: Glucose enters the blood. The brain, muscles, and organs all need it. Who uses it fastest?
example.solution: The brain uses ~20% of all glucose, always! Muscles use more during exercise. Energy is distributed by blood.

slides.inSimpleWords: Glucose powers your brain, muscles, and every organ.

image.alt: Tracking Nutrients — Human Body and Digestion

slides.title: Waste Leaves: The Large Intestine
slides.storyContext: What Priya couldn't be absorbed (fiber, water) continues to the large intestine. Here, water is reabsorbed, and waste is prepared to leave the body.

points.label: End of journey
points.text: Undigested material becomes feces, stored in the rectum, and excreted

slides.inSimpleWords: Indigestible waste leaves your body as feces.

image.alt: Waste Leaves: The Large Intestine — Human Body and Digestion

slides.title: Digestion Complete
slides.storyContext: Priya (rice grain) has become glucose, powered Arjun's body, and her waste has left. The complete digestive journey!

points.label: Mouth
points.text: Chewing + saliva break down food (30 seconds)

points.label: Stomach
points.text: Acid churns food into paste (2–4 hours)

points.label: Small intestine
points.text: Enzymes finish digestion + villi absorb nutrients (3–6 hours)

points.label: Large intestine
points.text: Water reabsorbed, waste prepared for exit (final stage)

points.label: Total time
points.text: Food takes 6–40 hours to complete digestion

slides.inSimpleWords: Your digestive system is an amazing processing factory.

image.alt: Digestion Complete — Human Body and Digestion
